scope_note: Second-pass public-evidence audit for NTT Silicon Valley SV1 at 1160 Walsh Avenue, Santa Clara. The review reconciles the planning-era 1150 Walsh address to APN 224-58-003; adds the finaled principal permit, its administrative job value, current operator specifications, emergency-generator authorization and the parcel's regular-bill payment history; and leaves supplemental bills separate to avoid double counting. Public sources still do not establish realized site employment or payroll, total project investment, supplier payments, project-specific community transfers, metered resources, or project-attributable public-service costs.

sources.title: Santa Clara County property-tax details — APN 224-58-003
sources.publisher: County of Santa Clara Department of Tax and Collections
sources.notes: The official parcel page identifies 1160 Walsh Avenue, TRA 007-000, and annual regular bills for APN 224-58-003-00. The normalized series sums the two paid regular installments for each fiscal year and excludes separately numbered supplemental bills to avoid overlap. A parcel payment spans multiple taxing jurisdictions and does not establish NTT's economic incidence or a fiscal net.

sources.title: Building permit BLD2019-53423 — 1160 Walsh Avenue
sources.notes: The official permit record is Finaled and describes a new four-story, base-isolated data center with mechanical, electrical, plumbing and site work. It reports job value of $125,405,765 and identifies DPR Construction Inc. as general contractor. Job value is an administrative permit amount, not audited expenditure, payment, local purchasing or total investment.

sources.title: Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center
sources.notes: The current operator page identifies 1160 Walsh Avenue and reports 16 MW of critical IT load and 64,000 square feet of data floor, plus closed-loop water cooling. These are capacity and area descriptors, not utilization, annual electricity, whole-building area, metered water or audited environmental performance.

sources.title: Board of Directors meeting agenda — Executive Officer's report
sources.publisher: Bay Area Air Quality Management District
sources.notes: The report states that an Authority to Construct issued April 2, 2020 for RagingWire SV1, a 27-MW Santa Clara data center, covering ten 3.5-MW emergency backup generators and one 1.1-MW life-safety generator. Authorization does not prove installation, operation, fuel use, run hours or emissions.

sources.title: Substation Service Agreement for the RagingWire data center
sources.notes: The signed agreement links the 1150 Walsh planning address to the RagingWire project, states anticipated maximum demand of 27 MVA, makes the developer responsible for actual station development costs and calls for an initial $450,000 developer contribution. The agreement does not disclose final project cost, completed payment total or same-scope annual public-service cost; no available direct metric safely represents the contribution.

sources.title: NTT Opens New Silicon Valley Data Center
sources.notes: The operator announced SV1's opening on April 13, 2021 and described the four-story, earthquake-base-isolated facility and its 16 MW capacity. It supplies no realized site headcount, payroll, capital outlay, supplier spend or local community transfer.

sources.title: Community partners: Collaborating with first responders in Silicon Valley
sources.notes: The operator describes hosting a Santa Clara Fire Department confined-space rescue drill at SV1. No cash transfer, in-kind valuation, participant hours or recipient accounting is disclosed, so no community-benefit amount is normalized.

sources.title: California Competes Tax Credit awardee list

sources.notes: The official awardee materials were searched for RagingWire, NTT, NTT Global and the Santa Clara address; no project-linked award was found. Absence from this searched program is not proof that every possible incentive is zero.

sources.title: NTT SV1 Data Center
sources.notes: The project page identifies RagingWire as client and describes civil engineering, surveying and construction-monitoring participation at SV1. It provides no contract value, payment, vendor geography at payment time or locally retained procurement amount.

project_updates.title: Project boundary and construction audit
project_updates.notes: City planning, CEQA, permit and Legistar records were searched by APN 224-58-003, 1150/1160 Walsh Avenue, PLN2018-13128, CEQ2018-01049, BLD2019-53423, RagingWire and NTT for 2018-2026. The finaled principal permit supplies a $125,405,765 administrative job value and DPR contractor identity; it does not supply audited outlays, equipment split, worker hours, payroll, supplier payments or local retention. Later tenant fit-out permits are not treated as separate buildings or added to the principal value.
project_updates.project_description: NTT Silicon Valley SV1 is a single four-story colocation data center operated by NTT Global Data Centers at 1160 Walsh Avenue in Santa Clara, California, on APN 224-58-003, which planning records also identify as 1150 Walsh Avenue. RagingWire began the project in 2018, the City later finaled the principal base-isolated-building permit, and NTT announced the 16 MW facility's opening on April 13, 2021. This account covers that building and parcel, not later tenant fit-outs or NTT's wider Silicon Valley portfolio.

project_updates.title: Fiscal audit — regular parcel bills verified
project_updates.notes: The county tax portal was reviewed for APN 224-58-003 across fiscal years 2017-2018 through 2025-2026. Nine paid regular-bill principals are normalized; separately numbered supplemental bills are excluded to avoid overlapping assessment events. Santa Clara budget, agenda, state California Competes and financing-record searches found the developer-funded Oaks Junction agreement but no project-specific tax-credit award, bond subsidy or same-scope net fiscal result.

project_updates.title: Operations audit — capacity is observed, employment remains forecast-only
project_updates.notes: NTT/RagingWire releases, current specification and careers pages were searched for SV1, Santa Clara, 1150/1160 Walsh, employees, jobs, payroll, wages, occupancy and revenue from 2018-2026. The 16 MW and 64,000-square-foot data-floor specifications are retained, while the existing up-to-40-job plan remains a pre-opening forecast. No realized site FTE, payroll, wage, rack occupancy, revenue or operating expense was found.

project_updates.title: Resource audit — capacity and cooling design do not establish consumption
project_updates.notes: Operator, City water/sewer, Silicon Valley Power, CEQA and air-district sources were searched for electricity, demand, PUE, water, wastewater, emissions, generator run time and renewable energy. The operator reports critical-load capacity and closed-loop cooling, the CEQA record retains a pre-opening water projection, and the air permit supplies a generator count. No site meter, bill, observed peak, annual kWh, realized PUE, water, sewer, emissions or renewable share was found; no capacity-to-consumption model is added.

project_updates.title: Community audit — activity found, quantified transfer not found
project_updates.notes: NTT/RagingWire community, ESG, press and local nonprofit searches used SV1, Santa Clara, donation, grant, volunteer, school, nonprofit and first responder for 2018-2026. An SV1 fire-department training drill is documented, but no project-specific cash amount, in-kind value, volunteer hours or recipient accounting was public. No community amount is inferred.

project_updates.title: Investment and public-cost audit — infrastructure agreement is not a fiscal net
project_updates.notes: Land-sale, deed, financing, construction, substation and City budget records were searched by address, APN, RagingWire and NTT. Public sources disclose land purchase without a primary-record price and a $450,000 initial developer contribution toward actual Oaks Junction station costs, but not total project investment, completed contribution total, annual City operating cost or project-attributable police, fire, road, utility, administrative or financing cost. Only a tax-equal break-even threshold is modeled; no net benefit is asserted.

project_updates.title: Supplier audit — participants are identifiable, payments are not
project_updates.notes: Permit, project-team, operator, carrier and contractor sources were searched for DPR Construction, BKF Engineers, Linesight, procurement, vendor, supplier, contract and payment. DPR is identified on the principal permit, and public project pages identify other professional participants, but no contract value, paid amount, supplier address at payment time or Santa Clara County retained share was found. The permit job value is not allocated among suppliers and no procurement multiplier is applied.
